LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity: For a channel W with finite input and output alphabets and a nonempty input alphabet, its capacity in nats is C(W) = supₚ I(X;Y). The supremum runs over all input laws p, with Y generated from X through W.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_channe: For any input law p of a finite channel W with nonempty input alphabet, its input–output mutual information is at most C(W).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_l: For a finite channel W with nonempty input alphabet, C(W) ≤ r if and only if every input law gives mutual information at most r.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exists_mutualInfo: For a finite channel with nonempty input alphabet, some input law achieves the supremum in the capacity formula, so its input–output mutual information equals capacity.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_n: The capacity of a finite channel with nonempty input alphabet is nonnegative.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_l: A finite channel with nonempty input alphabet A has capacity at most ln |A| nats per use.
A finite channel with nonempty input alphabet and output alphabet B has capacity at most ln |B| nats per use.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_c: Independently relabeling the input and output alphabets by bijections preserves the capacity of a finite channel.
Cascading a finite channel V after W gives a channel of capacity at most C(W).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.channelCapacity_m: Applying any deterministic function to the output of a finite channel gives a channel of capacity at most its original capacity.
